meta.title: How to set up the VPN — a step-by-step guide
meta.description: Setting up GnomeVPN on iPhone, Android, Windows, macOS, Linux and TV: install the app and add the subscription from one link in minutes.

title: How to connect
intro: There are three ways to connect to GnomeVPN. If you are not sure, take INCY: one free app for every device and every protocol at once.

ios.name: iPhone and Mac
ios.install: Open the App Store and install INCY. The app is free and needs no account of its own.
ios.copyLink: Open your account on this site, go to the Connect tab and press Copy INCY link.
ios.import: Open INCY, tap + and choose import from clipboard. The app recognises the link and adds the subscription itself.
ios.connect: Pick a country from the list and press connect. The first time, iOS asks permission to add a VPN configuration — allow it.

android.name: Android
android.install: Install INCY from Google Play. If Play is unavailable, the INCY releases page has an APK.
android.copyLink: Open your account on this site, go to the Connect tab and press Copy INCY link.
android.import: In INCY tap + and import from the clipboard. Easier still: tap the link on the site — it opens the app and adds the subscription for you.
android.connect: Pick a country and connect. Android asks permission to set up a VPN connection — confirm it.

desktop.name: Windows, macOS and Linux
desktop.install: Download the installer above: exe for Windows, dmg for Mac, deb or rpm for Linux.
desktop.copyLink: Open your account in a browser, go to the Connect tab and copy the link.
desktop.import: Start INCY, press + and paste the link. Add it as a subscription rather than a single server, so the server list keeps updating itself.
desktop.connect: Pick a country and connect. On Windows you will be asked to approve an elevation prompt — it is needed to create the network adapter.

tv.name: TV
tv.install: On Android TV install INCY from Google Play; on Apple TV from the App Store.
tv.copyLink: Typing the link on a TV remote is no fun: open your account on your phone and show the QR code on the Connect tab.
tv.import: In INCY on the TV choose to add a subscription and scan the QR code from your phone screen.
tv.connect: Pick a country and connect. From then on the tunnel comes up by itself when the TV turns on.

other.title: Another subscription app
other.intro: INCY is what we recommend, not what we require. Your subscription URL is a standard one, so any app that takes a subscription link reads it — the same servers, the same traffic counter, the same renewal date.

copy.title: Copy the subscription URL
copy.body: Open your account, go to the Connect tab and press Copy subscription URL. This is the plain https link — not the INCY one, which only INCY understands.

add.title: Add it as a subscription
add.body: In the app choose to add a subscription or profile from a URL and paste it. Add it as a subscription rather than a single server, so the server list keeps updating itself.

connect.title: Pick a server and connect
connect.body: Each country comes in several variants: Hysteria2 over UDP, VLESS + Reality over TCP and, on some servers, WireGuard. The app labels each entry with its protocol. Start with Hysteria2; if the network blocks UDP, switch to VLESS.

other.note: Whatever app you pick, the link stays yours alone. If it leaks, rotate it in your account and the old one dies at once.

wireguard.title: A WireGuard config
wireguard.intro: For people who prefer WireGuard, and for routers. Configs are made on your account's Connect tab, under WireGuard; each one is for one device and one country and takes a place in your subscription limit. WireGuard is blocked in Russia more often than the other protocols, mobile networks especially: if it will not connect, use INCY.
wireguard.cta: Create a config in your account →

windows.name: Windows
windows.create: On your account's Connect tab switch to WireGuard, pick a country, name the device, press Create and download the .conf file.
windows.install: Install WireSock Secure Connect from its official site — the link is in the app card above.
windows.import: Open WireSock and import the downloaded .conf as a connection profile.
windows.connect: Pick the profile and connect. In the profile settings you can send only chosen programs through the VPN and leave the rest direct.

phone.name: iPhone and Android
phone.create: Create a config on your account's Connect tab, under WireGuard. It is easiest on a computer, opening the QR code — or download the .conf straight to the phone.
phone.install: Install AmneziaVPN from the App Store or Google Play — the links are above.
phone.import: In AmneziaVPN choose to add a configuration: scan the QR code on the computer screen or open the .conf file.
phone.connect: Connect. On first launch the phone asks to allow a VPN configuration — accept.

other.name: macOS, Linux and routers
other.create: Create a config on your account's Connect tab, under WireGuard, and download the .conf file.
other.install: On macOS install the official WireGuard app from the App Store, on Linux the wireguard-tools package. Routers that support WireGuard (Keenetic, MikroTik, OpenWrt) need nothing extra.
other.import: In the app choose to import a tunnel from a file. On Linux put the file in /etc/wireguard/. On a router import the .conf where WireGuard connections are set up.
other.connect: Turn the tunnel on. On Linux: sudo wg-quick up followed by the file name without .conf.

incy.title: The INCY app
incy.body: One link from your account and the app has every country and every protocol. Works on phones, computers and TVs.

apps.title: Another subscription app
apps.body: Hiddify, v2rayNG, Streisand and others: the same subscription link, if you already have an app you like.

wireguard.body: A .conf file for WireSock on Windows, AmneziaVPN on a phone, the official WireGuard app and routers.
